title: Button hitbox misalignment in scrollable containers on iOS Safari and Firefox Android
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Several buttons inside horizontally and vertically scrollable containers are reporting tappable area misalignment on iOS Safari and Firefox for Android. Visual tap targets appear correctly sized but touch events register offset (often above the visible component) when the container has momentum scrolling or transforms applied. This looks like a combination of layout/transform rasterization differences and our compact token scale for dense rows.

Scope: Reported in Dashboard list (compact rows), Tables with sticky headers, and Small chart controls in mobile view. Seen on iPhone 12/13/14 with iOS Safari 16/17 and Firefox on Pixel 6 (Android 12/13). Desktop Safari occasionally shows hover/click mismatch when using trackpad gestures. Affects primary/secondary buttons and small icon-only buttons (24px/32px token sizes).

Reproduction steps: 1) Open staging.redwood.com/dashboard on iPhone 13 (iOS 17) in Safari. 2) Scroll the left list quickly to trigger momentum scrolling. 3) Tap the second row action (icon-only kebab menu). Observed: tap opens the kebab menu for the row above the tapped one. Expected: tapped row's menu opens. Alternative repro: open a table with sticky header and action column, scroll the table body and tap action.

Observed behavior details: - Offset is usually ~8–18px upward when container has just decelerated. - Issues correlate with elements that have -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch or 3D transforms on ancestor elements (we use translateZ(0) on some containers). - Increasing button padding mitigates but breaks compact density goals. - On Firefox for Android, offsets are less consistent but reproduce when nested scroll containers are present.

Initial investigation: - Engineering confirmed event coordinates (clientY) match visual position on the element in most frames but hit-testing returns the wrong target after a composite layer promotion. - Design reviewed token scales: compact-icon (24px) + hitbox padding 4px; effective tappable area is borderline for mobile (32px). - Hypothesis: GPU compositing + transform/overflow heuristic causes mismatch between painted layer and input coordinate mapping in some browsers.

Trade-offs and proposed approaches: 1) Soft fix (Design + CSS): add explicit hit-area pseudo-element (.btn::after) with position:absolute and pointer-events:none to visually expand hit area without changing layout. Pro: preserves layout and density. Con: pointer-events layering complexity; may still be affected by compositing. 2) Layout fix (Engineering): avoid transform/translateZ(0) promotions on scroll containers and revert to composite-friendly CSS. Pro: addresses root cause; Con: potential regression in rendering perf on heavy charts. 3) Accessibility-first (Design): increase minimum touch target to 36px for dense rows and collapse secondary metadata elsewhere. Pro: robust and accessible. Con: reduces density and may affect product SLAs for compact lists. 4) JS polyfill fallback: capture touch coordinates and dispatch to corrected target while smoothing with small debounce. Pro: can be scoped; Con: fragile and platform-specific.

Immediate ask: Triage and land a low-risk patch for next minor release that prevents user-facing mis-taps while we evaluate broader fixes.

References and artifacts: - Figma frames: https://www.figma.com/file/abcd1234/UI-Kit-Compact-Lists (commented frames: Row/Action-offsets) - Confluence writeup: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/UX/pages/98765/Mobile+Hitbox+Compositing+Issue - Staging repro (video): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1xyz-demo - Engineering thread: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/7892 (WIP patch) - Test matrix: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/compact-list-qa - Screenshot (annotated): https://drive.google.com/file/d/1annotated - Related linear tickets: ENG-41234 (runtime input mapping investigation), ENG-41902 (sticky header scroll repaint), PM-55621 (density guidelines review)
comments: 2026-03-10 Maya Chen: Initial discovery during compact-list QA sweep. Captured video repro and raised to ENG. Marking as P1 because multiple product flows affected (dashboards + tables).

2026-03-11 Arjun Patel: Verified repro on iPhone 13 (iOS 17). Took screenshots and attached annotated frames in Figma. Suggested quick CSS shim to expand hit area for icon-only buttons and test across browsers.

2026-03-12 Linh Nguyen (Engineering): Investigated with remote device. Found that when ancestor has translateZ(0) we sometimes observe a 2D->3D compositing layer offset on input mapping in iOS Safari. Filed ENG-41234 to track native-layer mapping investigation. Recommended temporary workaround: remove translateZ(0) for scrollable zones and test perf impact.

2026-03-13 Arjun Patel: Design proposal v1: apply .btn--touchpad {padding: 6px; margin: -6px;} via pseudo-element for icon buttons only in mobile breakpoint. Kept visual density by overlaying hit area. Documented in Figma. Asking Eng to validate pointer-events behavior.

2026-03-14 Jamie Ortiz (Accessibility): Suggest minimum tappable area 36px for primary actions. Concerned adding pseudo hit area may confuse screen reader focus order unless implemented with semantic button element. Recommend accessibility smoke test if we implement CSS shim.

2026-03-14 Linh Nguyen (Engineering): Quick experiment: removing translateZ(0) restored correct hit-testing on iOS Safari in our staging build but added ~6–8% frame drop in the chart-heavy dashboard. Created feature-flagged change in PR #7892 for controlled rollout.

2026-03-15 Arjun Patel: Based on engineering data and accessibility feedback, I'm drafting a hybrid plan: 1) Ship CSS pseudo-element shim for icon-only buttons at mobile breakpoints as a temporary fix (can be A/B tested), 2) Revert translateZ(0) in scroll containers behind a feature flag and run perf regression suite, 3) Post-cycle evaluation to adjust token density if perf-cost tradeoffs persist.
2026-03-15 Maya Chen: Updated acceptance criteria and added task to update the Design tokens doc and QA checklist. Scheduling cross-team review Monday 2026-03-16.
acceptance_criteria: Temporary CSS shim deployed behind feature flag and verified on iOS Safari 16/17 and Firefox Android: observed tap targets register correctly without visual layout shifts.
Accessibility smoke test passes: screen reader focus order unchanged and semantic button elements preserved.
Perf regression for revert of translateZ(0) measured and documented; no >10% P95 frame drop in main dashboard charts for rollout to 10% of users.
Design tokens doc updated to include compact-icon hit-area guidance and examples.
QA checklist updated with repro steps and device matrix for mobile hitbox issues.
